compactMembership.notes: Arkansas's reciprocity operates via listed state-by-state reciprocal agreements (17 CAR 210-509 plus the Board's own Reciprocal Agreements roster) under which an applicant must still be issued a distinct Arkansas license — not a single multistate license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact, e.g. the Nurse Licensure Compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating this reciprocal-agreement mechanism with a compact, matching the same reasoning already applied to Colorado's NERA-based reciprocity in colorado-journeyman.json.

reciprocityRules.value: Arkansas reciprocates ORIGINAL (non-reciprocated) journeyman electrician licenses from 17 states: Alaska, Colorado, Idaho, Iowa, Maine, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Vermont, Wisconsin, and Wyoming. A license that was itself obtained by reciprocity in the issuing state cannot be re-reciprocated into Arkansas — only an original license qualifies. Wyoming licenses reciprocate only if the applicant completed a USDOL-approved apprenticeship program of at least 576 classroom hours; no such extra condition applies to the other 16 states. Per 17 CAR 210-404(e)(2), the applicant must also hold the sister-state journeyman license in good standing, have held it for at least one year, and have been tested (examined) in that state.

history.reason: Initial population from the Board of Electrical Examiners' Reciprocal Agreements page (state lists, Wyoming condition) and 17 CAR 210-404(e)(2) (good-standing/1-year/tested conditions).

reciprocityRules.notes: The 17-state Journeyman list and the Wyoming-specific apprenticeship-hours condition come from the Board's own 'Reciprocal Agreements' page content (retrieved 2026-09-04, page is Cloudflare-protected against automated fetch — content obtained via direct browser access); the 1-year-held/tested/good-standing conditions come from the codified rules text, 17 CAR 210-404(e)(2) (see arkansas-electrical-board-rules). A separate, smaller 4-state Master Reciprocal Agreement list (Iowa, North Dakota, Oregon, Texas) governs MASTER-tier reciprocity, with a materially different asymmetric rule — tracked separately in arkansas-master.json, not conflated with this Journeyman-tier record.

endorsementRules.notes: Arkansas's own materials describe this mechanism as a 'Reciprocal Agreement' specifically (17 CAR 210-509; Board's Reciprocal Agreements page) — no separate 'endorsement' pathway or terminology was identified, matching the same finding already recorded for Colorado's NERA-based reciprocity in colorado-journeyman.json.

requiredExams.value: A written examination ($80 fee) is required for standard/apprenticeship-path journeyman licensure, per 17 CAR 210-403(a),(c). The rules do not state an explicit examination exemption for reciprocal journeyman applicants — unlike the exemption explicitly granted to specialist sign electricians under 210-404(i)(2) — so reciprocal applicants are inferred, but not explicitly confirmed, to still sit Arkansas's own journeyman exam.

requiredExperience.notes: For Arkansas's ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) journeyman licensure — not the reciprocity pathway — an applicant must either (a) complete a 4-year USDOL-approved electrical construction apprenticeship program, or (b) accumulate 8 years (16,000 hours) of electrical construction experience without an apprenticeship (17 CAR 210-404(e)(1),(3)). Recorded here in notes rather than the main value, to keep the reciprocity-relevant fact primary — matching the same pathway-distinguishing treatment already used in colorado-journeyman.json's requiredExperience field.

requiredEducation.notes: No standalone formal-education requirement distinct from the apprenticeship/experience pathways already captured in requiredExperience was identified — matching the same scope decision already made in colorado-journeyman.json.

endorsementFeeUsd.notes: Arkansas's rules do not define a distinct 'endorsement' or 'reciprocity issuance' fee separate from the standard $80 journeyman examination fee (17 CAR 210-403(c)) — and whether reciprocal applicants must even pay that exam fee is itself unconfirmed (see requiredExams). Not recorded here to avoid conflating the general exam fee with a reciprocity-specific fee, matching Colorado's own explicit 'NOT independently confirmed' treatment of this field in colorado-journeyman.json.
